text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince Hassan says during a visit to the Jordan Valley: "We seek development without discrimination."

- Parliament approves the reply to the throne's speech and delays discussions over the resignation of deputy Nazeeh Amareen who tendered his resignation over government's handling of civil disturbances last August.
- Jordan's Ambassador to Israel Omar Rifai calls on the Jewish state to implement the articles on water in the 1994 bilateral peace treaty.
- Israel releases Jordanian suspected of spying for Jordan.
- An imminent decision on the restructuring of car customs, no reduction in customs.
- Optimism prevails in the stock market, with prices rising 1.2 percent in turnover exceeding one million dinars.
- An initial accord reached to resolve the dispute between the electricity workers and Jordan Electric Power company.
- Crown Prince says the reduction in services for Palestinian refugees "harms our security."
- Misuse of credit cards is becoming rampant in Jordan.
- No more free telephone calls for civil servants.
